Groq fallback once the Gemini chain is spent or overloaded. On the same 29 apps it agreed with Gemini 72% of the time (13/15 on Gemini-high ones), with defensible disagreements and well-calibrated confidence ('low' on description-less apps) — far ahead of gpt-oss-20b (45%) and gpt-oss-120b (52%). Groq's free tier caps it on tokens: 8,000/min, 200,000/day, and above all 1,000 *output* tokens/min, checked against the request's requested output before it runs. With the pipe-string output format (~12 output tokens/app, measured 2026-09-27; 78% agreement with Gemini on 64 apps), batches are capped at 32 apps: on Groq's strict json_schema, qwen3.8-27b never returns more than 32 array items (finish_reason 'stop' at 32, ~470 output tokens, even when told the exact count — measured 2026-09-30), so larger batches paid input tokens for apps that never got an answer. 32 apps also fit well under a 950-token output cap. Pacing on both total and output tokens (with margins) avoids per-minute 429s. Reasoning 'none' (supported by Qwen, not gpt-oss) keeps output lean.

Not calibrated yet (added 2026-10-04) — enable once a --sample run agrees with Gemini Flash. Gemma 3 on the Gemini API free tier is announced at 30 requests/min and 14,400 requests/day, but 15,000 tokens/min: token-capped like Groq, not request-capped like Flash, hence token pacing with a margin (13,000) and 100-app batches (~830-token system prompt + ~45 input and ~14 output tokens per app, about 6,700 tokens a request). Gemma takes neither a system instruction nor JSON mode on this API (plainPrompt), so parseResults extracts the JSON from free text. If its quality holds, it's the biggest free volume of the list.

Mistral's free 'Experiment' tier: about 1 billion tokens/month with a low request rate (exact limits only shown in the console — check before raising requestsPerMinute), and it requires opting in to training on the prompts, acceptable here since they're public package metadata. Request-capped, so large batches like Gemini Flash.

Not calibrated yet (added 2026-10-04). NVIDIA NIM's build.nvidia.com API: 40 requests/min with no daily cap announced, but presented as a trial for evaluation and prototyping, with a credit system that's poorly documented — check on the account whether credits run out before relying on it. json_object rather than json_schema: NIM's support for the latter is unverified. Other open models on the same endpoint (Qwen, Nemotron, ...) are worth sampling too.

Not calibrated yet (added 2026-10-04). GitHub Models' free tier: roughly 150-1,000 requests/day depending on the model tier, and a small per-request token cap (about 8,000 in, 4,000 out), hence 80-app batches. Needs a GitHub token with the models:read scope in GITHUB_MODELS_TOKEN.

Disabled 2026-09-26: on 29 apps Gemini had already classified, it agreed only 45% of the time (6/15 on Gemini-high ones), mostly dumping into System Tools, and rated 'high' apps with no description at all — its confidence can't gate what gets applied. Kept on file for its Groq token-capped settings: 50 apps per request stays well under the 8,000 tokens/min cap, and 'low' is gpt-oss's minimum reasoning effort.
